source_read: Saved PubMed Central page text (PMC5209286, author manuscript), read in full: abstract, graphical-abstract legend, all sections, the Table (as text) and acknowledgments; reference list checked for the cited studies.

anchors.locator: Does Methamphetamine Cause Clinical Parkinsonism in the Human?, 2nd paragraph
anchors.note: California inpatient cohort followed for up to 16 years against a matched appendicitis group, with a cocaine group as drug control (not increased); cited to Callaghan et al. (2010) and (2012a), both co-authored by Kish. Utah HR 2.8 (CI 1.6–4.8; the interval's level is not stated). The same paragraph adds that only a very small proportion of people who use methamphetamine are later diagnosed.

for_senior_author: Risk of bias: reader 2 partly agreed, asking that one instrument be used across the narrative reviews; the editors' rule now applies the narrative-review checklist to all of them, and this card already uses it. The domain judgments are reader 1's (Kish 2017 was not among the five narrative reviews re-appraised today), and the overall 'high' was set by the editor from the 'high' search domain. Card unchanged.
not_added: Introduction, 1st paragraph: an all-cause standardized mortality rate of 4.67 in the authors' California cohort (Callaghan et al., 2012b): confirmed; second-hand and outside this card's questions.
